lines.text: Napoleon conquered half of Europe... and then lost a fight to bunnies.
It's July, eighteen-oh-seven. He has just signed a big peace treaty, and he wants to celebrate.
So his chief of staff, Berthier, plans a rabbit hunt.
There's just one problem. His men bought tame rabbits from local farmers. Hundreds of them. Maybe even thousands.
The cages open. The hunters raise their guns.
But instead of running away... the rabbits run straight at Napoleon.
They weren't scared. They thought it was feeding time.
At first, everyone laughs. Then the bunnies just keep coming.
They swarm around his legs. He swings his riding crop. His men try sticks and whips.
The Emperor of France retreats... to his carriage.
And the bunnies chase him all the way there.
Some accounts even say a few hopped right inside.
The story comes from the memoirs of General Thiebault, so it may be a little exaggerated.
But if it's true, the man who beat entire armies got chased off by hungry bunnies.
Eight years later, Napoleon met his Waterloo. But the rabbits? They got him first.
